prerequisites: Basic knowledge of materials science and polymers

learning_outcomes.text: Understand how the properties of composite materials are related to the properties of their constituent materials, and be able to calculate these properties using quantitative models.

Acquire knowledge about the constituent materials, production processes, and usage properties of composites, and support this knowledge with practical experience in manufacturing and testing composite materials.

syllabus_topics: Criteria for material selection in lightweight constructions
Fibers: principles for strong and stiff fibers, fracture of main fiber types (carbon, glass, aramid and polyethylene, natural fibers), their production method, microstructure and properties
Plastic matrices: brief explanation of specificity of plastics for composites, knowledge from Plastics course is assumed; brief reference to other matrices (metallic, ceramic)
The interface between fiber and matrix
Basic principles of micromechanics for fiber or particle reinforcements, and indication of applicability to all types of composites (polymeric, metallic, ceramic)
Micromechanics for composites with continuous fibers: stiffness and strength
Basic principles of mesomechanics, and indication of applicability to layered structures and textile reinforcements
Classical laminate theory: calculation of stiffness and strength of layered materials
Basic principles, and differences/similarities with plastics and metals
Production methods for thermosetting composites and thermoplastic composites
Overview of different composite 'semi-finished products' for composites with continuous fibers: textile preforms, impregnated mats, etc.
Specificity of non-destructive tests for composites
Determination of fiber volume fractions, etc.
Comparison of cost price, LCA with other material solutions
Impact of composites on the environment
Introduction to production and testing methods for composites

assessment_methods.method: Computer exercise using laminate theory software (orals)
Oral or written open questions (depending on group size)

assessment_rules: The exam is a closed-book exam where the formularium available on Toledo may be used. A computer exercise using laminate theory software must be completed during the exam, which is orally evaluated and counts for 30% of the grade. The other questions count for 50% of the grade and may be oral or written. The remaining 20% of the grade is earned through the practicum, based on small interim tasks and the final presentation. Attendance at the practicum is mandatory; absence may lead to grade deductions and exclusion from the exam. For resits, practicum points are included if they improve the total score; if they would lower it, they are not counted. If no practicum score was obtained, an exam question on practicum material will be asked, counting for 20% of the total, regardless of its impact on the score.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
